name: Fibrous Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Fibrous Dysplasia

criteria.description: Characteristic radiographic appearance of ground-glass bone lesions
Biopsy showing fibrous stroma with irregular woven bone trabeculae without osteoblastic rimming
Presence of bone deformity, pain, or pathological fractures consistent with fibrous dysplasia
Detection of activating GNAS gene mutation in affected tissue

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic radiographic lesions plus either histopathological confirmation or compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is supportive but not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bone deformity due to fibrous tissue replacement

occasional.symptomName: Nerve compression symptoms (e.g., vision or hearing changes)
Muscle weakness adjacent to affected bone

rare.symptomName: Malignant transformation of fibrous dysplasia lesions
Hearing loss due to temporal bone involvement
Visual impairment due to optic nerve compression

laboratory: Possible elevated alkaline phosphatase in active lesions
imaging: Radiographs showing ground-glass appearance of affected bone
CT/MRI demonstrating extent of fibrous tissue and bone deformity
genetic: Somatic activating mutations in GNAS gene
other: Histopathology showing fibrous stroma with irregular woven bone trabeculae lacking osteoblastic rimming

distinguishingFeatures: Well-demarcated lesion with sclerotic border on imaging
Different radiographic features including cortical thickening and bone enlargement

references: DiCaprio MR, Enneking WF. Fibrous dysplasia. Pathophysiology, evaluation, and treatment. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2005;87(8):1848-64.
Riminucci M, Liu B, Corsi A, et al. Fibrous dysplasia of bone in the McCune-Albright syndrome: abnormalities in bone formation. Am J Pathol. 1997;151(6):1587-600.

Shenker A, Weinstein LS, Sweet DE, et al. Severe endocrine and nonendocrine manifestations of the McCune-Albright syndrome associated with activating mutations of stimulatory G protein. J Clin Invest. 1994;93(3):1226-31.
